messages:
cassie (Support): FYI escalation from customer about region mismatch + high latency. They say Console shows region=us-west1 for their org but our serving logs show requests hitting eu-north1. Customer also sees billing entries for EU. They provided a repro and logs.

omar (eng-routing): can you paste the exact request id and a sanitized curl? need to check routing headers and any fallback behavior.

cassie (Support): pasted sanitized curl and one log line the customer attached:

```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' -H 'X-Region-Hint: us-west1' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
```

log snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T14:23:01Z] request_id=abc123 org=acme serving_region=eu-north1 routed_from=us-west1 latency_ms=512 status=200
[2026-03-12T14:23:02Z] request_id=def456 org=acme serving_region=eu-north1 routed_from=us-west1 latency_ms=731 status=500
```

cassie (Support): Customer says console UI (tenant settings + top-right badge) shows US-WEST and per-route analytics in console show majority in us-west. But traces and our edge logs show serving_region=eu-north1 for the affected times. They want to know why UI differs from logs.

jason (SRE): quick hypothesis: Console reads the org default_region field from control plane metadata (where tenant was provisioned). Metrics pipeline currently attributes requests to the "routed_region" stored by the LB, while runtime logs emit the actual "serving_region" once a request hits a replica. If a fallback/overflow path sends traffic cross-region, we end up with mismatched UX vs runtime logs.

omar (eng-routing): agreed. We introduced a change last quarter where the front-end shows the configured region (org.default_region) not the actual serving region to avoid confusing customers when we autoscale across zones. That decision now backfires when customers expect the console to reflect where requests actually served.

marta (Billing): important: billing uses the serving_region tag (we charge where compute runs). If the runtime shows eu-north1 then billing is correct — customer will be charged for EU compute. We need a list of request_ids/time windows to validate charges before making adjustments.

cassie (Support): shared a redacted list of ~40 request_ids and the time window in the private escalation ticket (pasted link to internal ticket). Customer included p99 graphs showing spikes during fallback windows.

omar (eng-routing): repro steps for us:
1) use a token scoped to an org with default_region=us-west1
2) generate a burst of concurrent requests from a us-west client to saturate the us-west serving pool (I can simulate locally)
3) observe routing decisions + logs: LB will set routed_from=us-west1 but runtime may respond from fallback eu-north1 replica and emit serving_region=eu-north1

jason (SRE): instrumentation check: our access logs include both fields but the console analytics job was only joining on routed_from. We'll need to change the analytics join to prefer serving_region when present, and update the console label to show "Serving region (actual)" + a small tooltip explaining "may differ from tenant default region during fallback".

omar (eng-routing): quick mitigation: update the control plane to surface both values in the UI and add a flag to show actual serving region for the last 24h. Longer term: route logic change to prefer intra-region capacity before cross-region fallback, and surface fallback triggers in logs.

marta (Billing): I'll hold off on manual billing adjustments until we validate that those request_ids are indeed charged to EU. If they are, we need to prepare a customer-facing explanation.

cassie (Support): action items summarized:
- omar: small UI change to surface serving_region alongside tenant default (P0 UI patch)
- jason: update analytics ETL to prefer serving_region for per-request attribution (P0)
- omar + jason: investigate routing policy tweak to reduce unnecessary cross-region fallback (P1)
- cassie: provide full list of request_ids + time windows to billing and eng (done in ticket)
- marta: review charges and prepare message if a credit is warranted (P1)

omar (eng-routing): assigning to me and jason. I'll open an internal PR to show both fields and link it here when ready.

jason (SRE): I'll add a short-term K/V mapping in the ETL to prefer serving_region if present. ETA a few hours to a day depending on QA.

cassie (Support): customer replied: "thanks, as long as we get a clear explanation and can see where requests actually served we'll be OK." They also asked for an SLA impact analysis and whether cross-region serving increases latency — noted.

omar (eng-routing): we've got the latency evidence in the logs (see latency_ms values). We'll include a short note about expected added RTT for cross-region fallback and that routing will be tuned.

marta (Billing): :eyes: I'll wait for the request_id list.

sre-bot: deploy queued: feature/ui-serving-region-flag -> staging (build 2147).

cassie (Support): great, thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated with the ETA and link to the internal ticket. :thumbsup:

omar (eng-routing): dropping a note: long-term we should log both a "routed_region_hint" (where LB thought it would go) and "final_serving_region" so we can always reconcile. I'll add to routing backlog. :+1:
